ai.description: This slender lizard reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It features a brownish-olive dorsum with a distinct pale lateral stripe and possesses four pairs of chin shields.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Takydromus haughtonianus* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct lateral white stripe, which is typically present in other Indian *Takydromus* species.
ai.habitat: The Goalpara Grass Lizard inhabits moist, tall grasslands and scrub forests in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas, typically at low to moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Goalpora Grass Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects among tall grasses and low vegetation during the sunlit hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Takydromus haughtonianus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Takydromus haughtonianus* is endemic to the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas, specifically occurring in Assam and Meghalaya at low to moderate elevations.
